tagline.text: Ten sweet days in May on the island of mangoes

location.label: Location
location.text: Throughout Guimaras Province (centered on the capital, Jordan, and the provincial capitol area)

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Mid- to late May (about 10 days; dates change each year)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–5,000 (1 night, 2 days from Iloilo, including lodging, meals and boat fares)

children.text: The Manggahan Festival is the biggest event of the year on Guimaras, the island of mangoes, held for about ten days in mid- to late May. It brings a mango eat-all-you-can, cultural performances from the province's five municipalities, an agricultural fair, and music and food events, alongside the province's founding anniversary.

The Manggahan Festival is the province's biggest annual event, held every May on Guimaras Island, a short boat ride from Iloilo. The name comes from the word for mango, and the whole province gets sweetly excited in May, when the mango harvest and the provincehood anniversary coincide. In 2026 the 34th festival ran from
, and the provincehood anniversary was reported as May 22. Reports gave slightly different opening days, such as the 15th, the 17th or a Friday.
The most popular program is the Mango Eat-All-You-Can. In 2026 about 18 tons of mangoes were prepared, five tons more than the year before. The fee is
, and each batch can eat as much as it likes for
30 minutes

. There are eight batches Monday to Thursday and eleven Friday to Sunday, with weekend sessions extended into the evening. Because it gets crowded, you are advised to reserve a slot through the official online system.

In addition, music shows and food fairs run every night, and the five municipalities of Buenavista, Jordan, Nueva Valencia, Sibunag and San Lorenzo each present performances showcasing their traditions and culture. An agri-eco trade fair, the Miss Guimaras pageant and a music festival follow as well. The five colors of the festival logo are said to represent the five municipalities.

Guimaras is known as the island of the world's sweetest mangoes, and the provincial government reported more than 100 million pesos in tourism receipts and about 40,000 visitors from this festival in 2025 (figures vary slightly between reports). It can be done as a day trip from Iloilo, which makes it an easy way to experience a Philippine provincial festival. Dates and programs change every year, so check the latest announcement from the Guimaras provincial government. During the festival, the island's mango farms and processed-goods shops are livelier than usual, and Iloilo residents regard this time as the signature season for a trip to Guimaras.
The signature event lets you eat Guimaras mangoes to your heart's content for
30 minutes
for a fee of

. About 18 tons were prepared in 2026, and the number of batches differs between weekdays and weekends. Weekends are especially crowded, so book online. It was reported that weekend hours were extended to 7 p.m.

Buenavista, Jordan, Nueva Valencia, Sibunag and San Lorenzo each present dances and parades that express their own traditions and identity. It is said that results of the cultural competition are announced on the final day.

blocks.title: Music and food fair every night

children.text: Throughout the festival, music performances and food stalls open in the evening. You can taste mango desserts and local snacks all in one place.

A fair gathering local farm products, processed goods and crafts is held, and it is a good place to find mango jam, dried mangoes and souvenirs. One report says sales at this fair in 2025 came to about 14.3 million pesos.
A beauty pageant held alongside the provincehood anniversary events, it adds plenty to the festival atmosphere. Check the on-site announcements for exact event times.
Guimaras became a province in 1992, and the festival commemorates this. 2026 marks the 34th anniversary. Sources give the founding date as May 11 or May 22, so follow local announcements.

Fresh mangoes as well as processed foods such as mango shakes, mango pizza, dried mangoes and mango jam sell in large numbers during the festival. It is also worth visiting the island's signature restaurants and the monastery gift shop.

items.title: 1 night, 2 days
items.subtitle: A festival trip across from Iloilo

children.text: Go from downtown Iloilo to Parola wharf and take a boat to Guimaras. Festival weekends bring many passengers, so leave early.
Get off at Jordan, drop your bags at your accommodation and check the day's event schedule.
If you have booked a mango eat-all-you-can time slot, go to the venue on time.
Have lunch at a restaurant in downtown Jordan, then browse the fair grounds and specialty-product booths in the afternoon.
Take a taxi or tricycle for an island tour and stop at one nearby attraction. If you have time, the Trappist monastery is close by.
Enjoy the food fair and music performances in the evening, then return to your accommodation.
Buy dried mangoes and jam as souvenirs and take a boat back to Iloilo.
Program times change every year, so the above is only one example.
Take a boat across from the wharf in Iloilo.
Join the mango eat-all-you-can at your reserved time slot.
Take care of lunch and souvenirs at the booths around the venue.
Check the time of the last boat and return to Iloilo.
A day trip suits just the tasting and the fair; if you also want to tour the island, you need one night.
Check the last boat time locally.
You cross from Iloilo City to Guimaras by boat. Bangka boats run from the wharf in downtown Iloilo toward Jordan and Buenavista, and the crossing is described as taking about
15–20 minutes
RORO boats from Lapuz in Iloilo to Jordan port are said to run at intervals of about
30 minutes to 1 hour
from early morning to evening. Schedules change, so check.
Fares differ between sources, with a range of about
listed. There have been fuel-related increases and an announcement of new fares in April 2026, so check the latest fare.
Whether boats operate from Ortiz wharf differs between sources, so confirm before you go.
On festival weekends passengers crowd in, and boats may stop when waves are high, so leave slack in your schedule.
There are direct flights from Manila to Iloilo International Airport (ILO). Airlines and times change by season, so check when you book.
From the airport, take a taxi or ride-hailing car to downtown Iloilo, then board a boat at the wharf. Travel time depends on traffic.
On the island, use tricycles, jeepneys and taxis. The five municipalities are spread widely, so it is hard to see them all in one day.
The festival is centered near Jordan, so staying in Jordan makes getting around easier.
The Manggahan Festival is held for about ten days in mid- to late
May

every year. In 2026 it ran from May 15 to 24, with the highlights on May 22–24. The 2027 schedule is not yet set, so use mid- to late May as a guide and check the provincial government's latest announcement.

May falls near the end of the dry season, so it is mostly hot and clear, and it is mango harvest time, which makes it the best season for the tastiest mangoes. The midday sun is strong, though, so you need a hat and water.

The island has small hotels, guesthouses and beach resorts, mostly around Jordan. During the festival many Iloilo residents come for day trips or one night, so rooms fill up fast and you should reserve early. You can also stay in Iloilo and make a day trip.

The star of the food is, of course, mango. You will see fresh mangoes, shakes, dried mangoes and jam, as well as creative dishes such as the island's own mango pizza. Seaside restaurants serve grilled fish and seafood at reasonable prices.

When choosing lodging, check whether it is close to downtown Jordan, and if it is a beach resort, how long it takes to get to Jordan. After the festival's night events, public transport may thin out, so if your lodging is far from the venue, decide on your way back in advance. Prices vary greatly by season and room type, so follow local announcements.

Many people take care of breakfast at the island's market or roadside stalls with simple bread, coffee and fruit. In mango season you can buy freshly picked mangoes cheaply at roadside fruit stands, so buy one or two apart from the tasting event and you can taste the differences between varieties.
Reserve a time slot for the mango eat-all-you-can through the official online system. Weekends in particular fill up early.
Festival dates and programs change every year, so confirm them through announcements from the Guimaras provincial government before booking lodging and boats.
Boats stop when waves are high, so leave slack in your return boat time.
Many events are held in the daytime, so bring a hat, sunscreen, water and comfortable shoes.
Eating a lot of mango at once can upset your stomach, so enjoy it slowly over the 30 minutes.
For souvenirs, dried products and jam with sturdy packaging are easier to carry.
It is known that bringing mangoes from outside the island into Guimaras is restricted under quarantine rules, so check the notices at the wharf.
Many stalls need cash, so carry small bills.
Buying souvenirs before you board the boat back to Iloilo means carrying less. Check quarantine rules for bringing them on a plane or abroad.
Official festival information is posted on the Guimaras provincial government's website and social media, so check again a few days before you leave.
Dates and programs change every year and differ between sources, so be sure to check the provincial government's latest announcement.
Wharves and venues get very crowded on weekends and near the closing. Move early.
Boats can be suspended depending on weather and waves. Wear a life jacket and leave slack in your schedule.
Watch out for pickpockets and lost belongings in crowds.
If you have a mango allergy or a sensitive stomach, skip the eat-all-you-can.
Roads around the venue may be closed, so taxis and tricycles take detours.
On rainy days, outdoor events may be canceled or rescheduled, so bring a raincoat and check on-site announcements.
An introduction to the island that hosts the festival. With the Trappist monastery, beaches and island-hopping tours, there is a lot to see, and it works well combined with the festival.
The gateway city for crossing to Guimaras; it is close to the downtown wharf, so it is convenient for lodging.
A Gothic-style church in Iloilo, a good stop before or after Guimaras.
A UNESCO World Heritage church south of Iloilo that can be combined into a one-day outing.
